exposure: Epidural analgesia with 0.1% ropivacaine with fentanyl
Epidural analgesia with 0.1% levobupivacaine with fentanyl
outcome: Labour characteristics (onset of analgesia, duration of Stage I, II, III labour, top-up requirements, oxytocin augmentation)
Neonatal outcomes (birth weight, Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes)
cohort: The study included 40 term parturients with singleton cephalic pregnancies in active labour.
finding: Ropivacaine-fentanyl and levobupivacaine-fentanyl epidural analgesia provide rapid, effective, and safe pain relief during labour with comparable maternal and neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was recorded, and vaginal delivery occurred in most patients, with no significant difference between the two groups.
followup_time: Immediate neonatal outcomes (Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes) and intrapartum maternal outcomes.
birth_weight: Mean birth weights were 2.80+/-0.28 kg (Group A) vs 2.71+/-0.26 kg (Group B).
gest_age: Mean gestational age was 39.01+/-0.68 weeks (Group A) vs 38.82+/-0.75 weeks (Group B).
